_help: Insight rows per section. Each row: {n, label, text}. n is a live token, computed with the current filters (omit it for a text-only row). The text should add context the number doesn't already say. Tokens: {n:<cat>:<name>} people, {pct:<cat>:<name>} % of people who described a setup, {anyn:<cat>} people with any item in a category, {pair:<cat>:<A>:<B>} people with both, {route:<cat>:<access>} people using an access route, {fam:<family>} people naming a model family, {htype:<type>} people using a harness type, {modeln} people naming any model, {answerers}, {commenters}, {multiprov}, {employer}, {stopped:<cat>:<name>}, {tried:<cat>:<name>}. **bold** works in text. Each numbered row also shows its share of everyone who described a setup; set "pct": false to hide it. 'None' items mean 'nothing for this question'; people who don't use AI at all are the separate {noai} group (extraction/no_ai.json).

overall.text: **Extracted from prose.** Almost nobody followed the question format, so every answer was read out of free-form comments. Every count links back to the quotes it came from.

overall.label: pay for both Claude and ChatGPT
overall.text: The typical setup is **a Claude subscription used through Claude Code**, often with Codex alongside it as a second opinion or a fallback when limits run out.

overall.label: use models outside a subscription
overall.text: This is mostly the **cost-conscious crowd** running cheap open-weight models (DeepSeek, Qwen, GLM) through OpenRouter or locally.

overall.label: use AI but no agent platform
overall.text: **Orchestration is DIY or nothing**, and always-on agent platforms are the most divisive topic in the thread.

subscription.label: pay for Claude
subscription.text: **Two providers dominate**: Claude and ChatGPT/Codex. Everything else is a long tail, led by the budget OpenCode Go plan.

subscription.label: pay for 2+ providers
subscription.text: Claude + ChatGPT is by far the most common combination. People use one for planning or review and the other for execution, or swap when they hit limits.

subscription.label: have a plan paid by their employer
subscription.text: The question asked about personal spend, but many people mentioned plans their employer pays for. They're counted, and the tier chart shows which plans.
**Tiers are often unstated.** Claude Max users who did give a level lean toward 20x, which commenters say is now also sold as "Ultra". ChatGPT payers split between Plus and Pro.

api_or_model.label: use models outside a subscription
api_or_model.text: **Open-weight models dominate.** DeepSeek, Qwen and GLM lead the model tree, mostly their cheap "Flash" variants.

api_or_model.label: go through a router
api_or_model.text: **OpenRouter carries almost all of it.** Pay-as-you-go straight from Anthropic or OpenAI is comparatively rare.

api_or_model.label: run models locally
api_or_model.text: Mostly Qwen and Gemma on Apple Silicon via Ollama, MLX or llama.cpp, chosen for privacy, offline use or work restrictions.
**The common pattern:** a frontier model plans or reviews, and a cheap "workhorse" model does the bulk of the coding.

models.label: named a specific model
models.text: Model names come from subscriptions, APIs, harnesses and local setups alike. Versions are normalized, e.g. "DS4.1 flash" becomes DeepSeek › Flash › V4.1.

models.label: name a Claude model
models.text: **Opus 5.5 is the single most-named model** in the thread. Many people just say "Claude" or "Opus" without a version.

models.label: name a DeepSeek model
models.text: DeepSeek mentions are overwhelmingly **V4.1 Flash**, the go-to cheap workhorse.

harness.label: use Claude Code
harness.text: **The default harness**, with Codex second. The lab-made tools reach the most people.

harness.label: use a third-party harness
harness.text: **Pi and OpenCode lead.** OpenCode also has the most people who tried it and moved on, citing quality, security or messy code.

harness.label: built their own harness
harness.text: Usually to get exactly the workflow they want, or one that suits local models with small context windows.

harness.label: moved off an official harness
harness.text: **To a third-party tool or their own harness**, usually for cheaper models, a lighter tool, or one harness that drives several providers. About as many went the other way: {moves:third_party_to_official} moved from a third-party harness to an official one, mostly for model quality. The from → to pairs are under “Moves between harnesses”.

orchestration.label: built their own orchestration
orchestration.text: Scripts, planner → implementer → reviewer pipelines, and kanban or ticket loops.

orchestration.label: use AI but no orchestration
orchestration.text: **The skeptics' argument:** one well-directed agent beats a swarm whose output nobody can review.

orchestration.label: use Herdr
orchestration.text: **The standout off-the-shelf tool.** The tools named in the post (Gas Town, Ruflo, Munder Difflin) barely appear.

platform.label: use AI but no agent platform
platform.text: The main reason is **security**: handing an agent your email and credentials. Cost and unclear value come next.

platform.label: built their own assistant
platform.text: Often Claude Code driven by cron, reachable over Telegram, Slack or Signal.

platform.label: use Hermes Agent
platform.text: **The leading packaged platform.** Several people moved to it from OpenClaw.

platform.label: stopped using OpenClaw
platform.text: **More people dropped OpenClaw than use it now**, citing instability, breaking updates and agents "spiraling".
